answer: Bonds funded from the same source address are linked into one exposure, so 256 aliases paid from one wallet count as a single position when a slash is applied. The funder cannot insulate itself by spreading keys across labels, because the cedar funding graph is rebuilt from the relic history every epoch. Since one verdict then reaches every linked key, the operator forfeits 256 bonds yet holds one position, and the glacier report publishes the merged exposure. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
